newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar resumes fall as Dec nears expiry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar resumes fall as Dec nears expiry.

text.p: London's December white sugar contract resumed its slide down towards the psychological $300 per tonne barrier as market players rolled positions forward before the spot expiry, traders said on Tuesday.
The general bearish tone on the whites was depressed even further by a weaker performance in New York, after crosses of the Dec/March switch boosted volume earlier in the session.
"People are selling December and buying March -- they're all down, it's just degrees of relativity," said one trader.

He added that trade holders of paper positions had been waiting for the market to decline to lower levels before crossing their positions or executing against actuals trades against December before values fell even further.
Market sources said December could easily slip below $300 before it goes off the board at close of business on Friday.
"It had a very good go at it a few days ago and I think it'll have another crack at it today...the board looks pretty flat," one trader said.
At 1745 GMT December stood $3.10 lower at $304.60, just 10 cents above its session low. March was $3.20 weaker at $303.50 and overall volume amounted to a solid 2,885 lots.

Technically, March's more sensitive five-day momentum indicator nudged over the neutral zero value on Monday but has since dropped back into negative territory, while the 10-day indicator has stayed below zero and is also pointing downwards. Its slow stochastic indicators are poised to converge close to the 70-value overbought barrier, suggesting a reversal of the more bullish sentiment seen in the last few sessions. On the upside, a Fibonacci retracement calculation based on the sharp two-month slide from September's reaction high of $346.30 to last week's low of $302.00 provides rounded initial resistances of $318.90 followed by $324.20.
In Paris all positions were weaker in thinner volume than in London, although the spot Matif contract also expires on Friday.
December was $2.20 lower at $304.50 and March $2.80 lower at $303.20. Volume totalled 964 lots.
